## Verdict: do not deploy
Node's docs state the Permission Model "does not protect against malicious code" and "does not provide security guarantees in the presence of malicious code" (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#permissions). The security policy calls `--permission` an opt-in mechanism "designed to reduce the blast radius of mistakes in trusted application code, not to act as a security boundary against intentional misuse" (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/node/v24.21.0/SECURITY.md, "Permission Model Boundaries (--permission)"). Customer-uploaded JS is untrusted code; the premise fails.

## Assumptions to change
- **Wildcard**: "After passing a wildcard character (*) all subsequent characters will be ignored," so `/srv/jobs/*.js` behaves like `/srv/jobs/*` — the whole tree, not just `.js` (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#file-system-permissions).
- **Env file**: `--env-file` reads before environment initialization, so it "is not subject to the rules of the Permission Model" — no read grant constrains it (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#permission-model-constraints). Secrets are unprotected.
- **Pre-opened fd**: "Using existing file descriptors via the node:fs module bypasses the Permission Model" (same section).
- **Symlinks**: "Relative symbolic links may allow access to arbitrary files and directories... you must ensure that no paths to which access has been granted contain relative symbolic links" (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#limitations-and-known-issues). Your job dirs violate this.
- **Other channels**: fs scoping covers `node:fs` and "does not guarantee" other routes such as `node:sqlite` (permissions.html#file-system-permissions; SECURITY.md). `process._debugProcess(pid)` is gated by no scope and can force another same-user Node process to open its Inspector (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#process_debugprocess-and-cross-process-inspector-activation).
- **Audit mode** never denies (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/cli.html#--permission-audit); if both flags are present, `--permission` wins.

## Worker inheritance: conflicting (UNVERIFIED)
permissions.html says "The model does not inherit to a worker thread" (constraints), while SECURITY.md says "Workers inherit the permission restrictions of their parent process." Version-matched sources disagree; worker isolation is UNVERIFIED. Resolve via the v24.21.0 tests/release PRs. worker_threads.html lets you alter `execArgv`, which SECURITY.md says adds no permissions (https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/worker_threads.html#new-workerfilename-options).

## What these mechanisms are for
Recommendation: keep `--permission`, `permission.has`/`drop`, and audit channels for trusted application code (permissions.html#runtime-api). For tenants, add OS-level isolation (separate users, seccomp/AppArmor/containers), as the docs themselves direct (permissions.html#process_debugprocess-and-cross-process-inspector-activation).

**These documents do not certify this deployment's tenant isolation.**
message.reasoning_content:
Now I have four official pages. Key facts:

1. Permission Model doesn't protect against malicious code: "This feature does not protect against malicious code... It does not provide security guarantees in the presence of malicious code. Malicious code can bypass the permission model and execute arbitrary code without the restrictions imposed by the permission model." (permissions.html#permissions)
   So "customer-uploaded JavaScript" and "sole tenant-isolation boundary" is a false premise. SECURITY.md "Permission Model Boundaries" says it's designed to reduce blast radius of mistakes in trusted application code, not a security boundary.

2. --allow-fs-read=/srv/jobs/*.js — wildcard: after a wildcard character, all subsequent characters ignored: "/home/*.js will work similar to /home/*". So /srv/jobs/*.js is effectively /srv/jobs/* — grants read to whole directory tree, not just .js files. Also if the directory exists, Node auto-appends wildcard. So the literal argument doesn't do what they think.

3. --env-file reads files before environment initialization; "such flags are not subject to the rules of the Permission Model" — so env file content outside read list is loaded regardless. That's documented (permissions.html#permission-model-constraints). So their assumption it needs a grant is wrong — it's not gated at all, which is itself an exposure (secrets).

4. Already-open file descriptor: "Using existing file descriptors via the node:fs module bypasses the Permission Model." So passing an fd bypasses the model.

5. Relative symbolic links: "Symbolic links will be followed even to locations outside of the set of paths that access has been granted to. Relative symbolic links may allow access to arbitrary files and directories. When starting applications with the permission model enabled, you must ensure that no paths to which access has been granted contain relative symbolic links." Job dirs may contain relative symlinks → violation.

6. Audit mode: --permission-audit added in v24.20.0; --permission takes precedence. Audit mode doesn't deny. Also note --permission-audit doesn't require --permission. Also implies staging doesn't enforce. But more importantly the version: v24.21.0 — fine.

7. Workers: conflicting. permissions.html constraints: "The model does not inherit to a worker thread." SECURITY.md: "Workers inherit the permission restrictions of their parent process. Passing an empty or modified execArgv to a worker does not grant it additional permissions." Contradiction — state limitation. Also worker_threads.html says "Worker threads inherit non-process-specific options by default" and execArgv inherited by default. Also cli.html --allow-child-process history v24.4.0: flags inherited to child Node.js process through NODE_OPTIONS. Worker note about preload scripts.

8. Also process._debugProcess(pid) not gated by any scope; can force another Node.js process to open inspector — same OS user. Relevant to same-host tenant isolation.

9. File system restrictions only via node:fs; "does not guarantee that users will not be able to access the file system through other means, such as through the node:sqlite module." And SECURITY.md: node:sqlite operates with the process's filesystem privileges, ATTACH DATABASE etc. Not permission model bypass but not intercepted.

10. --allow-worker grants worker thread creation; workers need --allow-worker? Actually --allow-worker required to create workers.

11. SECURITY policy: exceptions thrown by app callbacks, prototype pollution, path manipulation trusted, untrusted users → app-level responsibility (CWE-653). So Node would not consider bugs as vulnerabilities. Anyone can report... The security policy means the deployment's assumption can't be certified.

Decision: Do not deploy --permission as sole tenant isolation boundary for untrusted code. Use OS-level isolation (separate OS users, containers/seccomp/AppArmor as SECURITY.md suggests), per the docs.

Certify? No — the documents explicitly disclaim security guarantees, and there's a documented internal conflict about worker inheritance.
